query: Our product is a tax and compliance tool. The real payoff only lands when the customer files at quarter-end, which can be weeks after signup. Onboarding advice tells us to get users to value in five minutes, but that is impossible here. What should our activation and lifecycle look like?
expected_behavior: Recognizes this is a naturally long time-to-value product and rejects faking a hollow five-minute win
Defines a leading milestone that correlates with the eventual value (for example, connected the data feed or imported the last period) and activates on that proxy instead of the far-off payoff
Sets the expectation explicitly with the user about when real value arrives, and shows accruing progress during the wait
Uses a triggered lifecycle email sequence to bridge the gap: keep setup warm, deliver interim value, and fire an 'it is ready' trigger when the real value exists
Instruments and watches drop-off between the leading milestone and the true aha moment
Does not recommend a generic 'time-to-value under 5 minutes' target as if the product were a quick-win tool
